task: closed-loop driving of the RDR ALERT dialogue; capture the screen that follows it
result: DONE. The screen that follows the ALERT dialogue is a SECOND RED PANEL headed WARNING. Two branches, both measured: (a) square = Continue Without Saving -> WARNING 'Autosave has been disabled. You may enable autosave in the options menu.' with a Continue [X] row; (b) cross = Create A New Save Game -> WARNING 'This game saves data automatically at certain points. Do not switch off the power when the HDD access indicator is flashing. Autosave may be turned off at any time in the options menu.' with the three ALERT rows still drawn under it. Either branch then reaches the RDR key-art 'Loading...' screen and dies in the known null+0x10 SIGSEGV at guest 0x10 inside f_0053338c (exit -11).
key_finding: The ALERT was unreachable because the tree's default VFS carries THREE RDR saves: with them ListAutoLoad matches 3 and the title loads a save and drives into the world (the SIGSEGV). With dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata EMPTY, ListAutoLoad matches 0, the title draws its own ALERT and waits indefinitely -- no crash at all while it waits. One env var, PS3BASE_VFS_DIR, is the whole difference.
key_finding_2: Both prior 'fixes' (dev_flash and RoundGuard) were necessary but neither is sufficient to reach the ALERT: the save state is the gate I was missing, and it is a test-harness condition, not a runtime defect.
buttons: Read from the pixels, not assumed: Continue Without Saving = SQUARE, Create A New Save Game = CROSS, Retry = CIRCLE. Cross is NOT the first row.
